items.headline: Federal agents search Rep. Ilhan Omar's home
items.summary: Federal agents searched Rep. Ilhan Omar's Washington home on Monday as part of a criminal investigation, reportedly an immigration-fraud probe. Omar said she would not be silenced and accused President Trump of an intimidation campaign, and Democratic leaders condemned the search.

items.headline: Saudis investigate air-defense failure in Riyadh airport attack
items.summary: Saudi officials said an initial probe found Houthi drones preceded the cruise and ballistic missiles that reached Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport. Investigators are examining how the defense systems failed to stop the deadly attack.

items.headline: Kremlin welcomes U.S. diesel deal as backlash grows
items.summary: Moscow welcomed President Trump's deal to buy Russian diesel and his criticism of President Zelenskyy; the exports are small but would add revenue for Russia's war effort. A bipartisan group of senators and several U.S. allies are urging Trump to reverse the deal, saying it breaks a 2022 ban.

items.headline: UK says Iran almost certainly behind plot at U.S.-run air base
items.summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said a suspected plot against a U.S.-run air base in England was almost certainly directed by Iran's Revolutionary Guard. He described the plot as highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran.

items.headline: Judge orders cancellation of taxpayer-funded Trump TV ads
items.summary: A federal judge ordered the Trump administration to cancel its remaining taxpayer-funded TV commercials promoting the president's political message. The order comes weeks before the midterm elections.

items.headline: Hackers heat up fridges in French supermarkets
items.summary: Hackers raised refrigerator and freezer temperatures at hundreds of French supermarkets overnight, spoiling food. TIME reports the cyberattack was described as unprecedented.

items.headline: Indian opposition marches on Supreme Court over voter rolls
items.summary: Indian opposition parties marched toward the Supreme Court as protests escalated over voter-roll revisions that removed more than 130 million names. They say the changes favor Prime Minister Narendra Modi's party.

items.headline: Farm costs and tariffs strain rural support for Trump
items.summary: Farmers told TIME that beef imports, rising fertilizer and diesel costs, and tariffs are hurting their operations. They say the pressures are weakening rural support for President Trump ahead of the midterms.

items.headline: Old handwritten records reveal warming in the Congo Basin
items.summary: Scientists digitized thousands of handwritten weather records to fill a gap in long-term heat and rainfall data for the Congo Basin. The records reveal the scale of regional warming.

items.headline: AI-powered drones spread on Ukraine's battlefields
items.summary: Both Russia and Ukraine are now using drones equipped with artificial intelligence. A Ukrainian company that once made pet-monitoring cameras now puts AI image recognition on combat drones.

digest.overview:
Federal agents searched Rep. Ilhan Omar's Washington home on Monday in a criminal investigation, and Omar accused President Trump of intimidation while House Democratic leaders called it an abuse of power. A federal judge ordered the administration to cancel its remaining taxpayer-funded TV ads promoting Trump's political message. Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio are reportedly weighing whether to fire Kimberly Guilfoyle, the ambassador to Greece, whose lawyers deny wrongdoing. Elon Musk has given more than $276 million since July to help Republicans hold Congress, making him the largest known midterm donor. Nearly 40 new voting laws, mostly in Republican-led states, take effect for the midterms. The Pentagon raised its count of U.S. service members killed in the Iran war to 21.

Abroad, Saudi officials said Houthi drones preceded the missiles that hit Riyadh's main airport, and the Houthis fired another ballistic missile at it while warning the U.S. against intervening. The Kremlin welcomed Trump's Russian diesel deal and rejected Zelenskyy's proposal for a 60-day ceasefire followed by elections, while the EU adopted nearly 1,600 new sanctions listings on Russia. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said a suspected plot against a U.S.-run air base was almost certainly directed by Iran's Revolutionary Guard. South Korean President Lee Jae-myung said national interest comes first in the U.S. alliance, as Seoul's ambassador in Washington acknowledged U.S. concerns over intelligence cooperation. Hackers raised fridge temperatures at hundreds of French supermarkets, and fire destroyed Paris's oldest covered market. Indian opposition parties marched on the Supreme Court over voter-roll cuts, and a report warned of famine risk in parts of Sudan.

home.overview:
The Brewers took a 2–0 NLCS lead with a 7–4 win over the Dodgers, knocking out Yoshinobu Yamamoto in the third as William Contreras homered and Christian Yelich delivered a go-ahead two-run single; Game 3 is Wednesday in Los Angeles. Cleveland opened the ALCS by rallying past Tampa Bay 7–3, with Nathaniel Lowe's two-run single in the eighth breaking the tie, and Game 2 is tonight at Tropicana Field. On Monday Night Football, Josh Allen ran for 121 yards and the Bills beat the Rams 37–34 in overtime on Tyler Bass' 45-yard field goal despite Puka Nacua's 17 catches; a postgame punch by Alaric Jackson is under review. Week 6 kicks off Thursday with Seattle at Denver.

Coventry crushed Newcastle 4–1 to climb out of the Premier League drop zone, and Levante and Sevilla drew 3–3 in La Liga. The Champions League returns tonight with an injury-hit Man United at Atlético, Barcelona at Galatasaray and Arsenal hosting Lille, before Man City meet PSG and Roma host Real Madrid on Wednesday. Championship leaders Swansea visit Millwall tonight. In the KBO, Kim Do-yeong's eighth-inning homer gave Kia a 4–2 win over LG and the No. 3 seed, so LG host Doosan in Wednesday's wild card round.

brief: Kia beat LG 4–2 in the regular-season finale to clinch the No. 3 seed, as Kim Do-yeong broke a 2–2 tie with a two-run homer in the eighth, his 45th of the season.
KT Wiz finished first at 90-49-5, ahead of Samsung, Kia, LG and Doosan.
Seoul rivals LG and Doosan open the postseason in the wild card round at Jamsil on Wednesday; LG advance with one win or a tie, while Doosan must win twice.
The wild card winner visits Kia for the first round starting Saturday.

brief: The Brewers beat the Dodgers 7–4 in Game 2 to take a 2–0 NLCS lead, chasing Yoshinobu Yamamoto after 2 2/3 innings, his shortest start of the season.
William Contreras drove in the tying run in the first and homered in the fifth, and Christian Yelich's two-run single after Jake Bauers' 12-pitch walk put Milwaukee ahead for good.

Cleveland rallied from 2–0 down to beat Tampa Bay 7–3 in ALCS Game 1, with Chase DeLauter and José Ramírez collecting three hits each and Nathaniel Lowe's two-run single breaking the tie in the eighth.
Shohei Ohtani went 0-for-4 in Game 2, and reports say the Dodgers are considering benching him as the series moves to Los Angeles.
ALCS Game 2 is tonight at Tropicana Field with Parker Messick facing Freddy Peralta, and NLCS Game 3 is Wednesday in Los Angeles.
